text: KDD is a feedback loop: something learned at a later step, such as pattern evaluation, sends you back to an earlier step such as cleaning or selection.
CRISP-DM runs business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, and deployment, and data preparation takes most of the time.
Spark beats MapReduce on speed because it keeps working data in memory across a cluster; PySpark is its Python API and needs Java underneath.
On a new computer, uv sync builds .venv from uv.lock, so every machine gets the same package versions.
An array holds one dtype, so mixed input converts every value to a common type: ints with floats become float64, and anything with text becomes text.
Pick the creation function from the job: zeros, ones, or full for a filled grid, arange for a sequence, eye for an identity grid, empty for a buffer you overwrite, random for placeholder data.
The _like functions copy the source array's shape and its dtype, unless you pass dtype yourself.
Passing dtype converts the values: int drops the decimal part toward zero, and bool is False only for zero.
type() names the container, .dtype names the type of every element, and .shape gives the length along each axis.
